prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: COc1ncc(-c2ccc3nccc(-c4ccnnc4)c3c2)cc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1F
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL4005

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of PI3Kalpha (unknown origin) using PIP2 as substrate after 1 hr in presence of ATP by kinase-glo luminescence assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of PI3Kalpha (unknown origin) by ADP-Glo assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.62, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 for PI3Kα inhibition using closely related luminescence-based kinase activity readouts (Kinase-Glo detects remaining ATP, ADP-Glo detects produced ADP), both are binding/functional assays with confidence score 9, same target and organism, so results are expected to agree within ~0.3 log units despite the slightly different detection chemistries."}
